title: DROP TABLE
description: DROP TABLE removes a table and every row in it, permanently - there's no undo outside of a backup. Drop the `appointments` table.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: DROP TABLE
DROP TABLE takes just the table name - no WHERE clause, because it's removing the whole table, not filtering rows out of it.
Use DROP TABLE followed by the exact table name, appointments.
expected_behavior: The appointments table no longer exists.
explanation: This exercise runs inside a rolled-back transaction like every other one here, so it's completely safe to practice - in a real database, DROP TABLE is one of the few commands worth pausing before you run.

hidden_tests.check_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = 'fixtures' AND table_name = 'appointments'
hidden_tests.label: appointments table is gone
